meta.notes: Repo moved from sst/opencode to anomalyco/opencode in early 2026.
meta.tldr:
OpenCode 2.2.2 introduces significant quality-of-life improvements, most notably enabling image generation by default. When a connected provider supports image models, agents can now use `experimental_image_generate` without any extra configuration, with the preferred model configurable via `experimental.image_generate.model`. This streamlines workflows for developers leveraging AI for visual content.

Desktop users will experience faster navigation with direct worktree selection from the new-session screen by clicking the Git branch. The UI for quotes and annotations has been unified across the timeline, terminal, and browser, now sharing a compact optional-comment editor, while source highlights remain local. The classic question cards are now the default, with the redesigned keyboard-oriented dock accessible through **Settings → Experimental → New question UI**. Desktop also sees a new side-panel tab menu with visible close buttons for overflowing tabs, compact user-message actions, and a redesigned active todo pill for clearer task visibility. Consistent styling has been applied to searchable dialogs and composer pills.

Core improvements include recording the start time of each session’s latest execution and better handling of persistent terminal requests and media preservation during session forking or import. TUI bug fixes address truncated paths, improve Go usage-limit messages with reset times and account links, and correctly type and display Go and ChatGPT usage-limit errors. The SDK now offers `if` and `until` inputs for `client.experimental.schedule.create`, exposes `SessionInfo.time.busy` for execution start times, and allows optional source metadata for prompt file attachments. Extensions benefit from optional `title` and `subtitle` fields for composer notes, source-relative quote positioning, and focus options for composer integrations. This release is recommended for all users to benefit from enhanced usability and stability.

breaking_changes.title: Automatic OpenCode updates removed
breaking_changes.description: OpenCode updates are no longer installed automatically. Users must now manually trigger updates or upgrades using the new `/update` command in the TUI or `opencode upgrade` CLI command.
breaking_changes.migration: To update OpenCode, use the `/update` command within the TUI. To upgrade to OpenCode 2, use `opencode upgrade --major` from the command line.

breaking_changes.title: Session Sharing Discontinued
breaking_changes.description: Session sharing functionality has been completely removed. This means existing share links are no longer valid, session-sharing commands are unavailable, and importing sessions from share URLs is no longer supported.
breaking_changes.migration: Users who relied on session sharing will need to find alternative methods for collaborating or sharing session content, such as exporting session transcripts manually.

breaking_changes.title: @opencode/ai root is now the Promise API
breaking_changes.description: `@opencode/ai` now works like `@opencode/sdk` and `@opencode/client`: the package root exports the Promise API, and the Effect API moved to `@opencode/ai/effect`. `@opencode/ai/promise` is removed, and the wildcard subpath export is replaced with an explicit list of provider and protocol entry points.
breaking_changes.migration: Change `import { AI } from "@opencode/ai/promise"` to `import { AI } from "@opencode/ai"` and `import { LLM } from "@opencode/ai"` to `import { LLM } from "@opencode/ai/effect"`.

breaking_changes.title: The OpenCode GitHub Action is removed
breaking_changes.description: The OpenCode GitHub Action is no longer published.
affected: GitHub Actions workflows using the OpenCode GitHub Action
breaking_changes.migration: Remove the OpenCode GitHub Action from your workflows.

breaking_changes.title: TUI plugins require OpenTUI 0.7
breaking_changes.description: `@opencode/plugin` now requires `@opentui/core` and `@opentui/solid` 0.7.0, up from 0.6.8 or later. Plugins that depend on OpenTUI 0.6 fail to install until they upgrade. In OpenTUI 0.7, custom renderables read their hooks from their class at construction: assign `renderBefore`, `renderAfter`, and `onLifecyclePass` in the constructor instead of as class fields, call `refreshHooks()` after adding a hook by reflection, and replace `defineNativeIntegration()` with a `static nativeIntegration` declaration.
breaking_changes.migration: Upgrade `@opentui/core` and `@opentui/solid` to 0.7.0. Update custom renderables to assign hooks in the constructor, call `refreshHooks()` after adding hooks by reflection, and use `static nativeIntegration` instead of `defineNativeIntegration()`.

breaking_changes.title: `@opencode/ai` Provider Removals and Renames
breaking_changes.description: Several providers and legacy entry points have been removed or renamed within the `@opencode/ai` package. This affects code that directly imports from `@opencode/ai`.
affected: fal provider and `./providers/fal` entry point removed.
Black Forest Labs provider and `./providers/black-forest-labs` entry point removed.
Replicate provider and `./providers/replicate` entry point removed.
Stability provider and `./providers/stability` entry point removed.
Legacy entry point `./providers/amazon-bedrock-mantle` removed, replaced by `./providers/amazon-bedrock/mantle`.

Legacy entry points `./providers/google-vertex-chat`, `-interactions`, `-mistral`, and `-responses` removed, replaced by `./providers/google-vertex/chat`, `/interactions`, `/mistral`, and `/responses` respectively.
Provider `configure()` input types renamed from `Provider.LanguageModelOptions` to `Provider.Config` (e.g., `Groq.LanguageModelOptions` → `Groq.Config`).
`model()` settings are now optional when every setting is optional.
breaking_changes.migration: Update imports for removed providers and legacy entry points to their new, nested paths. Adjust `configure()` input type names to `Config` for affected providers. Review `model()` calls where all settings are optional.
